sources.text: Afshari Lab Corneal & Ocular Surface Research Laboratory Advancing research in corneal regeneration, stem cell biology, oxidative stress, genetics, cataract prevention, and dry eye disease. Our lab studies the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying corneal and ocular surface disease, with the goal of developing new strategies to preserve and restore vision. Natalie A. Afshari, MD, FACS Professor of Ophthalmology · Stuart I. Brown, MD Chair in Ophthalmology in Memory of Donald P. Shiley Chief of Cornea and Refractive Surgery · Vice Chair of Ophthalmology Research Focus Four questions guide our work Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy causes the cornea’s hexagonal endothelial mosaic to break down cell by cell. We approach that breakdown from four angles at once: genetics, cell biology, environmental injury, and surgical outcomes. 01 — Genetics Fuchs Dystrophy Genetics Genome-wide association studies identifying the loci that drive Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy, and CRISPR/Cas9-based strategies targeting the toxic RNA repeat expansions implicated in disease. 02 — Cell Biology Endothelial Regeneration Deriving corneal endothelial cells from pluripotent stem cells and studying endothelial wound healing and migration, including ROCK-inhibitor pathways that promote cell spreading after injury. 03 — Environmental Injury Oxidative & Toxic Stress Modeling smoking-related oxidative injury to the endothelium across species and screening candidate therapeutics, including FGF10, alongside studies of autophagy under pharmacologic stress. 04 — Surgical Outcomes Cataract & Corneal Surgery Cost-effectiveness and outcomes research on intraocular lens selection, endothelial preservation during cataract surgery, and emerging roles for AI in surgical planning. From the Lab Imaging the endothelium A sample of the microscopy behind our research — from the native hexagonal cell mosaic to live-cell migration and molecular markers of proliferation and stress. Native endothelial mosaic The hexagonal cell mosaic of the healthy corneal endothelium — the structure lost in Fuchs dystrophy. Endothelial wound migration Live-cell imaging of endothelial cells migrating to close a wounded region of the monolayer. LC3 / DAPI, drug-treated Autophagy marker LC3 (green) and nuclei (blue) across control and drug-treated corneal cell conditions. Cultured endothelial cells Fluorescence imaging of corneal endothelial cells in culture. Autophagic puncta Punctate autophagy marker staining used to assess cellular stress response. Selected Publications Recent & representative papers Dr. Afshari is author of more than 200 peer-reviewed publications and co-editor of a two-volume cornea textbook.
